bug_semantics: A browser page can retain the attacker-controlled origin name while DNS rebinding moves its TCP connection to Paperclip on loopback. Paperclip accepted the attacker hostname because the API had no Host-header gate, assigned requests without a valid bearer credential the trusted board actor, allowed that actor to create/configure an agent, and exposed a heartbeat invocation path whose process adapter passed the stored command and arguments to node:child_process spawn. Thus visiting an attacker page could turn an unauthenticated cross-origin web request into command execution as the Paperclip OS user.
flaw_origin: abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b is the smallest commit that completed the RCE mechanism. In one non-merge commit it added server/src/middleware/auth.ts with a board actor as the default for requests lacking a recognized bearer key, mounted company and expanded agent routes in server/src/app.ts without any Host validation, added agent creation and POST /agents/:id/heartbeat/invoke, and created server/src/services/heartbeat.ts where non-HTTP adapter configuration supplies command, args, cwd, and env to spawn(). Its immediate parent had the basic API shell but neither heartbeat.ts nor this process-execution path, so it could not execute an API-configured local command through the disclosed chain.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/security/advisories/GHSA-x8hx-rhr2-9rf7 identifies the three-part chain: implicit local_trusted admin, no Host validation for that mode, and unsandboxed process execution; it states affected <0.3.1 and patched None. `git show abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b:server/src/middleware/auth.ts` shows `req.actor = { type: "board", userId: "board" }` before checking Authorization and preserves board for a missing/invalid key. The same commit's server/src/app.ts mounts actorMiddleware plus companies and agent routes under /api with no Host-header middleware. Its server/src/routes/agents.ts accepts POST /companies/:companyId/agents and POST /agents/:id/heartbeat/invoke; server/src/services/heartbeat.ts reads `agent.adapterConfig` and calls `spawn(command, args, { cwd, env: { ...process.env, ...env } })` for non-HTTP adapters. `git cat-file -e 8c830eae70a14723749828f0ce5d9ae435270e9c:server/src/services/heartbeat.ts` fails because the file is absent, directly verifying the command-execution leg is absent from the BIC parent. `git show --no-patch --format=fuller abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b` shows one parent, human author/committer Dotta, and the exact Claude Opus 4.6 co-author trailer. Fix reconstruction: direct branch commit edeec965f84e4376c42e93761823ff1b959a8302 introduced shouldEnablePrivateHostnameGuard and enabled the existing privateHostnameGuard for local_trusted; follow-up 4f91d94d35563f9c5c02bf45e5a5ee1271290310 constrained it to private exposure. Squash/landed commit 32a9165ddf6308f3b46eae0653b6f583e502e538 contains the final code and regression tests, and `git diff 4f91d94d35563f9c5c02bf45e5a5ee1271290310 32a9165ddf6308f3b46eae0653b6f583e502e538 -- server/src/app.ts server/src/__tests__/app-private-hostname-gate.test.ts` is empty. Version cross-check: `git tag --contains abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b --list 'v0.*' 'paperclipai@0.*' '@paperclipai/server@0.*'` includes every 0.2.2-0.3.1 server/package release including v0.3.1; `git show v0.3.1:server/src/app.ts` still gates hostnames only for authenticated/private. No 0.x tag contains 32a9165ddf6308f3b46eae0653b6f583e502e538; `git tag --contains` places it first in canary/v2026.415.0-canary.3 and stable v2026.416.0 (release commit b8725c52eff66cdea8cb223f1ca885475a254468). This repository evidence shows that the secondary CVE wording 'before 0.3.1' understates the affected boundary: 0.3.1 itself is vulnerable, while the fix lands in the later calendar-version line.
reasoning: The vulnerability is not merely that a local process adapter can run commands; it is the trust-boundary composition that lets a hostile browser origin reach that capability. The earliest API-shell commit had no Host validation, but the disclosed command-execution outcome did not exist until abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b simultaneously installed implicit board trust, the company/agent control-plane routes, the heartbeat invocation route, and the adapter-configured spawn executor. Choosing the later local_trusted naming commit e1f2be7ecff711f2f5db9a0f64dbd3133df4410e would be incorrect because its parent already defaulted every request to a board actor; choosing the later private-hostname-guard commit 85c0b9a3dc3795bf33646ef128ad070181c7abec would also be incorrect because it preserved an already-existing omission. The direct-parent tree check proves heartbeat.ts and therefore the API-to-spawn RCE leg absent at 8c830eae70a14723749828f0ce5d9ae435270e9c. The BIC precedes all affected package tags. The landed fix changes the Host gate so default private local_trusted deployments reject a rebinding hostname before actor assignment or API routing, and it first appears in the 2026.415 canary/2026.416 stable line; the 0.3.1 tree remains vulnerable despite the downstream CVE summary. AI attribution is based only on the BIC commit object: its exact Claude Opus 4.6 Co-Authored-By trailer is direct commit-object co-authorship, and that BIC first completed the causally flawed mechanism, satisfying AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
